A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PMPD research, and their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison. Retained material can be matched despite relocation and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-task evaluations, scheduler ablations, GPU kernel measurements and NPU simulations, including additional experiments in its appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds phase-allocation comparisons, larger-model evaluations, end-to-end GPU speedups and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: Phase-aware precision allocation, progressive precision lowering, both schedulers, the attention-plus-MLP architecture and cross-entropy training are retained. The main-text scheduler formula restates Appendix A.1; output-length terminology and dimensional corrections refine the specification without establishing a different implemented method.

E1.justification: Both use C4 for scheduler training and CNN/DM, Dialogsum, IWSLT French-English and MT-Bench for evaluation. The larger-model experiments reuse existing datasets, and the added MT-Bench examples do not establish new task or input-environment coverage.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain their single-precision baselines, DNS comparisons and random-scheduler controls. The new larger-model and end-to-end GPU tables reuse established uniform-precision comparators; they introduce no new comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendices A.2–A.4 add a reversed phase-allocation control, Static-scheduler evaluation on Llama3-8B and Longchat-16k-13B, and whole-model GPU latency speedups on RTX 4090 and A40. These extend the experimental settings while retaining the original benchmark protocols and kernel measurements. Detailed timing procedures for the new end-to-end results are not supplied.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a direct comparison of increasing prefill precision versus increasing decoding precision. Appendix A.8 adds one successful and one unsuccessful MT-Bench output. Existing scheduling, phase-allocation, scheduler-feature and alternative-quantizer analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both report average GPU kernel timing over 100 forward passes. v2 adds no seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained, including original appendix Tables 4–6, now Tables 7–9. New Tables 4–6 substantially expand findings with phase-allocation scores, 8B/13B model results and end-to-end GPU speedups of 1.74–3.36 times versus fp16. Appendix A.8 adds qualitative outcomes. The new 2-bit MT-Bench score of 18.3 differs from the retained Table 2 score of 16.7 without an explained setting difference, so it is not an established same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1.1 corrects the learned query's dimension from Dv to Dk, consistent with multiplication by the transposed key cache. The scheduling horizon is clarified from maximum context length CL to maximum output length OL in the bounds and candidate grid. The optimization objective and combinatorial reasoning otherwise remain.

C1.justification: The abstract newly states up to 1.41 times GPU speedup over uniform quantization, alongside the retained fp16 and NPU comparisons. The three principal methodological contributions and the conclusion remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 explicitly interprets the added experiments as evidence of applicability across model scales. Appendix A.8 acknowledges that coherent generation can still fail to answer a mathematical question. Existing mechanism explanations, distribution-shift discussion and GPU-launch bottleneck limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code repository link in the abstract, providing access information absent from v1. Existing quantization, scheduler-training and GPU/NPU implementation details are largely retained; the PDFs alone do not establish the repository's contents.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Llama 3 model card and the Longchat-related context-length paper to support the larger-model experiments. The related-work discussion and positioning against previous quantization and precision-adaptive approaches remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and part of the introduction are condensed, the scheduler formula is also presented in the main text, and publication/header wording is updated. Four appendix subsections are added and existing ones renumbered, while the main narrative structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds three appendix tables and formatted output examples, relocates existing tables and adjusts surrounding layout. The seven existing figures are retained. Caption edits include correcting Phi-1.5 from 2/4 to 3/4 bits in Table 1, matching the entries already present in v1.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens validation through end-to-end GPU measurements absent from v1, a direct prefill-versus-decoding control, larger-model results and an explicit failure example. Mathematical corrections and code-access information also help. The improvement is limited by sparse documentation of the new latency measurements and the unexplained 18.3 versus 16.7 MT-Bench baseline difference between Tables 4 and 2.
